_doc: THE OPEN-PR HANDOFF RECORD. What a manager arriving COLD needs to know about every
PR in flight that it did not open.
WHY IT EXISTS. Measured 2026-09-02T06:17Z while checking whether a manager handoff
would actually work: SESSIONS.json carried ZERO structured PR fields and 19 rows
mentioning a PR only in PROSE, and nothing anywhere mapped a PR to its owning
session, its blocker, or the operator decisions already attached to it. A cold
manager would have had to grep prose.
⚠️ THE DANGEROUS CASE IS NOT A FORGOTTEN PR -- IT IS A FORGOTTEN APPROVAL.
#10746 carries a Tier-2 operator approval that is CONDITIONAL (stage on bybit_1,
NOT a fleet-wide flip). A manager that does not know the approval exists stalls and
re-asks, which is merely wasteful. A manager that knows it was approved but NOT the
condition could merge it fleet-wide onto a real-money account. Those are opposite
failure modes and only the second is dangerous, which is why `operator_decision`
records the CONDITION and not just the verdict.
⚠️ THIS FILE IS WRITTEN BY HAND AND GOES STALE THE MOMENT A PR MERGES.
It is NOT the source of truth for PR state -- GitHub is. Read it for OWNERSHIP,
INTENT and DECISIONS, which GitHub does not carry; re-read CI and mergeability from
the API before acting on any row. `as_of` is when a human last touched it.
MI-43 is building the check that refuses a handoff when this is stale.
⚠️ `operator_decision` IS A TYPED OBJECT AS OF MI-43, NOT A STRING.
{verdict, condition, scope, decided_on, text}. `verdict` is a closed vocabulary --
approved | approved_with_conditions | not_required | pending | none_recorded --
and `text` MUST carry the operator's original wording VERBATIM so the typed verdict
stays checkable against what was actually said. scripts/ops/open_pr_record.py
--strict FAILS a row whose verdict is `approved_with_conditions` while recording
neither `condition` nor `scope`: that row reads as approved, which is the
half-informed state that could merge a demo-only approval onto a real-money account.
⚠️ WHAT THAT DOES **NOT** CATCH, SAID PLAINLY: an author who writes
`verdict: approved` where the operator actually attached conditions. Nothing inside
the repo can detect that -- knowing a condition was given requires knowing what the
operator said, and THIS FILE IS THAT RECORD. The typed form narrows the failure from
'a condition silently absent from prose nobody parses' to 'a verdict field a reader
can compare against `text`'. A narrowing, not a closure.
maintained_by: the manager session holding the lease
source_of_truth_note: GitHub is authoritative for state; this file is authoritative for ownership, intent and operator decisions.

⚠️_the_last_row_is_always_stale_and_that: A handoff can never reach open_prs=PASS at the exact moment of the final merge, and this is a PROPERTY of the design rather than a bug to chase. Every open PR must have a row; the PR that prunes the last stale row is itself an open PR and needs a row; merging it makes THAT row stale. The regress terminates only if the manager stops opening PRs. ⚠️ DO NOT 'fix' this by exempting the currently-merging PR from the completeness check — the exemption would be indistinguishable from the real failure it exists to catch (a PR nobody recorded), and a check that cannot tell those apart is worse than the transient row. The correct reading: at handoff, `open_prs` naming ONLY the PR being merged right now is materially ready; naming any OTHER pr is not. State which case you are in rather than quoting the verdict alone.
⚠️_a_row_can_UNDER_claim_and_no_check_ca: Found 2026-09-02 on this very row. `open_pr_record.py --strict` grades a verdict that DECLARES conditions and records none — the over-claiming direction, which is the dangerous one. It cannot catch the OPPOSITE: I typed #10758 `none_recorded` while a full operator decision, with its condition, sat in MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json under MI-34 the whole time. `none_recorded` is a valid verdict needing no condition, so the row passed every check while being simply wrong. ⚠️ The cost is real but is NOT symmetric with the over-claiming case: a successor reading `none_recorded` re-asks the operator — wasteful and SAFE — where one reading a bare 'approved' could merge a demo-only Tier-2 approval onto a real-money account. So this is worth KNOWING, not worth a new failing check: cross-checking every row against the checklist would fire on the many PRs that legitimately have no decision anywhere. The mitigation is the reviewer's, not the guard's — read MANAGER-CHECKLIST for the PR's item before typing `none_recorded`.

settled_prs.title: ⛔ TIER-2, HELD: move the hourly work digest onto the VM's own clock (MI-83)
settled_prs.tier: 2 — MERGING IS THE VM MUTATION. install_systemd_units.sh globs deploy/*.timer, so the next deploy installs and enables ict-work-digest.{service,timer} on the live trader. There is no separate install step to gate on.

operator_decision.text: AWAITING ONE OPERATOR OK: install a new hourly systemd timer on the live trader. The unit runs a read-only digest render plus ONE local file write into the bot's ping inbox — no order path, no strategy config, no risk cap, no broker call, no network. ⚠️ THE MANAGER DID NOT KNOW THIS PR EXISTED until 21:12Z, ~15 min after it was opened, and found it only by polling its author's session summary — which is BL-20260902-SESSIONS-REGISTRY-HAS-A-SPAWN-WRITER-AND-NO-CLOSE-WRITER-SO-EVERY-ROW-READS-WORKING demonstrating itself a second time inside one evening.

settled_prs.blocker: ⚠️ DO NOT MERGE WITHOUT THE OPERATOR'S TIER-2 OK — the merge IS the install. ⚠️ AND DO NOT 'SIMPLIFY' IT by calling work_digest.py --write from the timer: that latch is DAY-granular and inert in CI (runtime_logs/ is gitignored, so a fresh runner never has the file), so it would silently cap an hourly carrier at one digest per day with no error. tests/test_work_digest_hourly_carrier.py::test_the_runner_does_not_share_work_digests_day_granular_latch is what stops that, and it is deliberately behavioural. ⚠️ work-digest.yml's schedule: block deliberately STAYS until a scheduled firing is observed — the accepted cost is ~5 duplicate digests a day, which is a KNOWN STATE, not a defect to re-file.

settled_prs.title: [RECOVERED — DO NOT MERGE] MI-56 AVAX venue-max work orphaned by a dead session

operator_decision.text: No operator statement exists. ⚠️ THE ROW MATTERS MORE THAN THE PR: this branch preserves ~320 lines of UNREVIEWED order-path work (execute.py, qty_legalize.py, precision.py) recovered from a DEAD session's uncommitted working tree. It must NOT be merged on green CI — its existing venue-max tests monkeypatch _resolve_venue_lot_rule to return vmax=22_000, so they exercise the CLAMP and never the RESOLUTION, i.e. they pass for the wrong reason, which is how the AVAX leg reached a third recurrence. A successor reading 'draft, CI green' without this row could land unreviewed order-path code on a real-money client.

settled_prs.blocker: Needs a live session to take ownership and verify the resolution path against a real venue read, then re-open as a normal Tier-gated PR. Until then this branch is a BACKUP, not a proposal.
settled_prs.disposition_basis: ESTABLISHED FROM PRIMARY SOURCES 2026-09-03T13:5xZ, NOT INFERRED, and NOT INVENTED to satisfy a guard. THREE independent readings agree: (1) the PR's own TITLE is '[RECOVERED — DO NOT MERGE]' and its body calls itself 'a preservation commit, not a proposal' — it was a backup of ~320 lines that existed only as uncommitted working-tree changes in a dead session's container, and its Test plan reads 'Not run. Deliberately. Running CI on this would invite reading green as approval.' It was never intended to merge. (2) Its own Disposition section asked for 'a live session to take ownership ... and re-open as a normal Tier-gated PR'. (3) That happened: MI-90 records the work re-opened as #10900 and MERGED on the operator's Tier-2/3 OK, after the recovered diff was read adversarially — 6 recovered tests fail on main and pass on the branch, and the ceiling was confirmed as the venue's own (Bybit named max_qty 22000, bracketed by an accepted fill at 21657.1 and a rejection at 22995.1). So the content LANDED by another route and the backup was closed. ⚠️ WHY THIS ROW MATTERED FAR BEYOND ITSELF: its missing `disposition` was the single fact jamming `open_pr_record.py --strict`, which is what fails every `reconcile-open-prs` automation PR — 7 open as of 13:45Z, with a new one generated on EVERY merge to main. Measured directly by running the failing guard against #10938's own OPEN-PRS.json: one finding, this row. See MI-103. ⚠️ AND THE GUARD WAS RIGHT TO REFUSE. 'superseded', 'the operator refused it' and 'the author gave up' are opposite next actions, and only the first is true here — reading it as either of the others would have sent someone to re-litigate a Tier-3 order-path change the operator already approved.

settled_prs.title: MI-101: make the close-wedge ledger's ABSENCE unreadable as a clean fleet

operator_decision.text: Operator approved in-conversation at the day manager's wind-down, 2026-09-03, verbatim: 'ok, approved'. UNCONDITIONAL — no account scoping, no staging, no soak was asked for, and none is recorded here. ⚠️ RECORDING `approved` RATHER THAN `approved_with_conditions` IS A POSITIVE CLAIM THAT NO CONDITION WAS GIVEN, not the absence of one being written down: a row asserting a verdict whose condition was dropped is worse than a missing row, because it reads as complete. The operator had been shown, in the checklist item and in this record, that the digest will report NOT EXAMINED until the trader restarts — that is a stated CONSEQUENCE of the change, not a condition on it.

settled_prs.blocker: ⚠️ NEEDS THE OPERATOR'S ONE TIER-2 OK. It makes src/runtime/close_wedge_standing.py's monitor sweep WRITE where it previously returned early. ⚠️ AND IT HAS A VISIBLE OPERATOR-CHANNEL CONSEQUENCE THE SUCCESSOR MUST NOT BE SURPRISED BY: until the trader restarts with the heartbeat, the work digest will report NOT EXAMINED instead of today's false clean bill. That is the honest state of a ledger nothing writes, it is strictly more informative, and it self-resolves on the next deploy — it is NOT a regression to roll back. Opened ready, not draft; the declaration holds it, not the draft flag.
